notes: The assigned description names a placebo control condition. The original Study 1 instead uses natural variation in bar-goers’ alcohol consumption, with each participant answering switch and footbridge dilemmas. The locator p. 3 supplies both BAC correlations and does not establish which outcome corresponds to this assigned row. No target is assigned by row order, numeric matching, or replication condition. Candidate original Study 1 final participant count is explicitly 60, after one exclusion for not following instructions (61 recruited); this is not an assigned placebo/dose subgroup N and is retained only for parent field-scope review. Candidate same-test pairs on PDF p. 3 / printed p. 123: footbridge BAC correlation r = .29, p = .023; switch BAC correlation r = .17, p = .17. Table 1 on PDF p. 4 / printed p. 124 instead prints switch-BAC .18, while footbridge-BAC is .29*. The prose/table discrepancy is preserved; neither switch coefficient is selected. The source specifies that each Study 1 participant responded to both dilemmas. No effect conversion or N derivation performed. Rendered PDF pages 3 and 4 inspected for layout. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
